chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from 'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'When a man performs the obligatory eight circuits around the House and is certain of eight, he adds six to them; and likewise, if he is certain that he has performed eight sa'is, he adds six to them.' If he performs the eight circuits deliberately, he must repeat the sa'i, and we have explained that; and if he performs nine circuits, it is not obligatory upon him to repeat the sa'i, and if he wishes to build upon what he added, he has done so.

key_terms.سَعَى: performed Sa'i (running between Safa and Marwa)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim is unsure whether they completed eight or fewer circuits during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the Shia jurisprudence regarding doubt (*shakk*) in the number of circuits during Hajj or Umrah, distinguishing between deliberate error and uncertainty. It establishes that while deliberate omission of circuits requires repeating the *sa'i*, uncertainty allows for adding six more runs to complete the ritual, reflecting the principle of building upon the probable. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on precision in ritual worship while providing practical leniency for common pilgrim errors.
